learning_outcomes.text: Understand the specific technical documentation and theoretical bases on the methodology for industrial design.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve industrial design problems using specifically established methods.
Be able to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs of industrial systems and components that meet specific requirements.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve industrial design problems.
Function effectively both individually and as a team.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
An adequate knowledge of their engineering branch including some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
The understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.
Function effectively both individually and as a team.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to comply with the required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply current legislation as well as specifications, regulations and mandatory standards in the field of mechanical engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge and skills to apply graphic engineering techniques.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to industrial design and product design
Machine and tool safety and regulations: Product safety, CE marking, Risk assessment and Machinery Directive
assessment_rules: To pass the course, the student must obtain a total score equal to or greater than 5. In the ordinary call, the final grade will be the sum of continuous assessment (4 points) + the ordinary final exam (6 points). Continuous assessment consists of a practical computer exam for CAD-CAM-CAE (2 points) and a partial exam of completed topics (2 points). In the extraordinary call, the final grade is the greater of two options: either the extraordinary final exam on 10 points, or continuous assessment (4 points) + the extraordinary final exam on 6 points (with a minimum of 4 out of 10 required for the second part questions/exercises). Laboratory practices are mandatory and assessed (completion of practice and submission of report).
